items.title: Harold Danko interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 28, 2021
items.q: There are some tapes that I have that are very precious where John sounds kind of like Paul Desmond.

ctx.x: Well I’m wondering, when did the idea of playing, creating music from chord changes come — when were you confronted with that?

Well the legend in my house is that my brother Joe early on in the Swing Era, because he started playing in clubs back when he was about 12 or 13, back in the war years because, in the second World War. So he started making good money, and the legend in the house was that he traded in some of my dad’s polka records for a Benny Goodman record. And so that brought jazz into the house. And there was still enough polka records laying around, so jazz was in the house and between my brother Joe, who was older and very…
Um hum. There’s a lot to be said for playing by ear, isn’t there?
